newsitem.title: UK: First Leisure to invest 55 million stg.
newsitem.headline: First Leisure to invest 55 million stg.

text.p: First Leisure Corp confirmed on Thursday that it planned to invest 55 million stg in new units in 1996/97.

The bingo, bowling and nightclubs group said trading in the early part of its new financial year had generally been in line with the second half of last year. But it had been hit by cold weather in the important period just after Christmas.
The company said it looked to the medium and long term with confidence and said new investments should underpin a significant growth phase into the next century.

First Leisure reported a nine percent increase in pre-tax profit to 43.7 million stg in the year to October 31. Excluding the benefit of asset disposals, pre-tax profits were up eight percent at 42.1 million stg.
The company said it planned a major expansion programme in nightclubs with six openings lined up for this financial year.
Its Health & Fitness development programme was reported to be making "significant progress" and contracts have been signed for eight new openings.
Excellent results were reported from the Brannigans Music Bars and a significant expansion programme was continuing there. But trading in bingo and theatres fell below expectations.

"These (record profits) are driven by excellent results in our three largest divisions where our previous investments have borne fruit as consumer confidence has recovered," chairman Michael Grade said in a statement.

"Our developing Bingo business has not yet met our profit expectations but this has been balanced by accelerated progress in a number of other new areas, including the expansion of the Brannigans Music Bar chain and our Health and Fitness clubs."
